newsitem.title: USA: US Plains see warmer weather, E. Midwest colder - WSC.
newsitem.headline: US Plains see warmer weather, E. Midwest colder - WSC.

text.p: Lows in the U.S. Central Plains overnight Wednesday were not cold enough to damage the winter wheat crop, but freezing temperatures are seen in the eastern Corn Belt Thursday night, a U.S. meteorologist said.

"In the winter wheat belt, low temperatures ranged from 28 (degrees Fahrenheit) in northwest Kansas to mostly the 30s to mid-40s otherwise," said Joel Burgio, senior meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass.
Temperatures in the eastern Corn Belt are expected to drop "well down" into the 20s in Indiana, Ohio and Michigan overnight Thursday, Burgio said.
The colder weather could discourage some farmers from planting, but producers will be able do fieldwork because showers over the next several days will be light, Burgio said.
"It does turn quite cool over the eastern Belt, but I don't think that would be a major deterrent to field work, but it will be rather cool," Burgio said.
A few showers are expected in the northwestern and far northern Corn Belt on Friday, and showers are seen in the southern and western Midwest on Saturday, Burgio said.
On Sunday and Monday, showers are forecast to move from west to east through the southern portion of the Corn Belt.
Long-term forecasts show much below normal temperatures headed for the Central Plains winter wheat belt by the end of next week, Burgio said.
"The next couple of days will warm up considerably, but there are hints we might see colder weather late next week," Burgio said. "It does bear watching."
Long-range charts for the Midwest also suggest moderate to heavy rains late next week.
"The end of next week might be a very wet period for the southern and eastern Midwest," Burgio said.
